clue.text: Holiday firm supplies oysters

parts.note: Whit, short for Whitsun, is a Christian festival and traditional British holiday
firm means steady, stable

explanation.surface: A travel company provides oysters as part of its package.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITSTABLE is a town on the Kent coast famous for its oysters; 'Holiday firm' looks like a travel company but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent seaside town is renowned for its oyster beds, so it is a place that supplies them.

clue.text: Cape being blown in the wind?

definitions.meaning: a headland at the southern tip of South America, Cape ___
a brass instrument blown in an orchestra's wind section

explanation.surface: A headland battered by gales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Horn is the famous headland, and the instrument is blown in the wind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Tone taken by doctor in fatigue

indicators.note: in signals that the doctor is placed inside the word for fatigue

parts.note: to fatigue is to tire
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's manner is affected by his own exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tone quality or colour of a sound or voice.

clue.text: Soldier on a horse or ship

explanation.surface: A soldier choosing between riding and sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry private is called by this name, and so historically is a troopship.

clue.text: Entice one into a club

indicators.note: into signals that the letter for one goes inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Lure someone into joining a society.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait is to lure or tempt, as with food on a hook.

clue.text: It takes pluck to remove it

definitions.text: It takes pluck to remove it

parts.words: It takes pluck to remove it
parts.note: pluck seems to mean courage, but it is plucking with tweezers that removes facial hair above the eye

explanation.surface: Removing something requires bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairs above the eye are commonly shaped or removed by plucking with tweezers.

clue.text: Drunk crashed in a single seater

indicators.note: drunk suggests these letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk driver smashed up in a one-person vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single seater' suggests a racing car, but the answer is the old enclosed chair carried on poles by two bearers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat for one person carried on poles.

clue.text: Christian virtue fills a need, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A Christian virtue meets a need in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-denial, restraint of one's own desires, is prized as a Christian virtue.

clue.text: We hear top player is to step down

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is to be said out loud

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: Gossip says a leading sportsman is going to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or yield a position, so to step down from it.

clue.text: One may be uplifted by ship on the equator

parts.note: a tramp is a cargo ship with no fixed route
the equator is the line at zero latitude, so 0 for zero followed by LINE

explanation.surface: A vessel sailing at the equator lifts someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors call the equator 'the Line'; it lies at latitude zero, giving O before LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast is bounced high into the air by a sprung canvas frame.

clue.text: Perform in pantomime horse perhaps? That creates interest

parts.note: to be is to act or perform a role
a pantomime horse costume holds two actors, each one half of the animal

explanation.surface: Acting in a two-person horse costume makes people curious.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime horse is a British Christmas-show costume worn by two actors, front and back, so each is half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Behalf means interest or benefit, as in acting on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Proverbially thickset

parts.note: split as thick set: the proverb says close friends are as thick as these villains

explanation.surface: A stocky build, as the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'as thick as thieves' makes these robbers a proverbially close-knit group.

clue.text: Novice nurse employed with the infantry

parts.note: a tender is one who looks after or nurses
foot soldiers are the infantry

explanation.surface: A trainee nurse working alongside foot soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or beginner unused to hardship.

clue.text: Conspicuous at a court hearing

definitions.meaning: presented as material for the court to consider at a trial

explanation.surface: Standing out in a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means noticeable, and literally also describes exhibits produced before the court.

clue.text: Sort of net used by French watermen

definitions.meaning: a large fishing net hanging vertically with floats and weights
the river through Paris, navigated by boatmen

explanation.surface: A kind of fishing net favoured by French boatmen.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a type of dragnet and the great river of Paris.

clue.text: A singular spectacle

parts.note: spectacle seems a sight, but here means an eyeglass, and singular means just one of them

explanation.surface: A remarkable sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass is in effect one lens of a pair of spectacles.

clue.text: The boy came up to me for reward

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, came up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster approached me to collect a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is an award given as a reward for achievement or bravery.

clue.text: Replace French man with Welsh

parts.note: Rene is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: Swapping a Frenchman for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to replace something worn out with a new one.

clue.text: Left a long time back — Christmas maybe

indicators.note: back signals the long period is read in reverse

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time

explanation.surface: Something left behind ages ago, perhaps at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another word for Christmas, especially in carols.

clue.text: Transport will be back at eleven

indicators.note: back here means the little word at is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A ride home arranged for eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a form of transport.

clue.text: Go quietly to spill the beans

definitions.meaning: to tell tales, inform on someone

explanation.surface: Slip away silently to reveal secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneak is both to creep furtively and, in schoolboy slang, to tell tales.

clue.text: Sloppy hands act sycophantically on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard ship, so the second word goes inside the letters for a steamship

parts.note: aboard ship: SS, steamship
to crawl is to grovel or fawn

explanation.surface: Sloppy deckhands suck up to their superiors on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' looks like crew, but it means handwriting; 'on board' places a word inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawls are untidy scribbled handwriting, a 'hand' being a style of writing.

clue.text: Pink gin ordered for a VIP

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are rearranged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drink requested for an important guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the most important person in a group, a very important person.

clue.text: Building uninsured if I cease to provide cover for it

indicators.note: the run of words covers the answer, which is concealed within them

explanation.surface: A building left uninsured if I stop paying for its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building.

clue.text: No mean party?

explanation.surface: A generous party.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means generous, and the Liberals are a British political party.

clue.text: Torpedo carriers ordered to base

indicators.note: ordered means these letters are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Warships sent back to port.
explanation.definitionFit: E-boats were German motor torpedo boats of the Second World War.

clue.text: Feast I set out for a religious festival

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A feast laid out for a religious celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival, especially a saint's day in Spain.

clue.text: There's beer and the last of the cognac for him

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: the last of picks the final letter of the brandy's name

explanation.surface: Drinks set out for a man in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' needs the clue's whole sense: a man's name, short for Alexander.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a man's name, so the clue's him is a fellow called that.

clue.text: Endless danger for a fairy

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: peril is danger

explanation.surface: A fairy faces unending danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology.

clue.text: Oil rig sited in a good position

parts.note: an oil rig sits over an oil well
placed means sited

explanation.surface: An oil rig located in a favourable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-placed means advantageously situated.

clue.text: One hundred in it is twice reduced by 50%

indicators.note: in signals that the letter for a hundred goes inside the word one

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A puzzling sum in which a hundred is halved and halved again.
explanation.walkthrough: Two times a half equals one time: halving 'twice' leaves the single occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Halving 'twice' leaves just one occasion, a single time.

clue.text: The cricketer makes another mistake

definitions.meaning: a close fielder beside the wicketkeeper in cricket
a further slip, an additional error

explanation.surface: A cricketer errs again.
explanation.definitionFit: Second slip is a cricket fielding position, and also a second error.
